inputs.text: The organizers’ claim of 8 million people at more than 3,300 “No Kings” events is an estimate, not evidence that the country has rejected President Donald Trump. A crowd can make noise; it cannot replace an election or speak for millions who chose a different direction. Calling political opponents a danger to democracy is a familiar way to dress up partisan hostility as moral authority. If these protesters want change, they should persuade voters and respect the lawful institutions that preserve order—not pretend that their own demonstrations confer a mandate.

output.main_topic: The “No Kings” protests do not confer an electoral mandate
